decisions.summary: seat_cluster refuses a margin whose outward normal is more than 45 degrees off the wind (WIND_BACK_MIN_DOT = cos 45), recorded at the constant as a map convention.

decisions.summary: A margin under the bar is kept in an offwind list, used only when no wind-facing margin (clean or divided, in D3's order) can be taken; recorded as meta.seat_offwind; the pool test fails any pool map that carries it.
decisions.why: Unchanged decision; the previous ruling stands. Where no wind-facing margin survives the seat's hard constraints the literal rule is physically impossible, and the alternatives are no map or renaming the wind - the behavior the GM asked to end. The wind is never renamed, the belt's side stays the northwest, the departure is recorded on the map, and test_pool_wind.py forbids seat_offwind on every pool map (shipped manifests: false on all five). The previous round's note that the XVI row wrongly said 'no exception' is now answered: the row records the fallback and that it is raised with the GM in the hand-off. For that hand-off: R4 measures its reach outside the pool - 22 of 48 cohort seeds seat off-wind under this order, 10 with belts under 50 clumps and 4 with none - which the GM should be told in those numbers.

decisions.summary: Clean wind-facing, then clean off-wind (seat_offwind), then - only when every margin is divided - the best divided margin, wind-facing first. Feature 230's strike-out outranks the wind.
decisions.why: Unchanged decision; the previous ruling stands. Where FR-004's wind-facing clause and FR-010's strike-out cannot both hold at a seed, the alternative order (a wind-facing divided margin ahead of a clean off-wind one) was refused twice in MODE 1 and measured over the 48 cohort specs (R4): 12 divided seats, 3 with a byre, well, garden or fixtures across the brook from their houses - feature 230's own failure, which FR-010 forbids - against 0 under this order. The spec's remedy for the pool is re-seeding (D4), enforced by the pool test. The previous round's finding is answered: D3's evidence paragraph now rests on R4 and its figures (12 divided, 3 across the brook, none under this order; 22 of 48 off-wind, 10 belts under 50 clumps, 4 with none) match R4's table; the overstated 'four of twelve' and '250-odd clumps on 29 of 30 Sawada seeds' are gone. The diff changes only that paragraph.

decisions.summary: Sawada 6 -> 24, Mizuguchi 23 -> 27 and now Kashikawa 3 -> 8, declared fall, sink, brook flank and household count kept, reason in each generator's docstring; seed 8 chosen over 14 because 14's belt wrapped 333 degrees round the houses; the pool test holds the belt's arc to 200 degrees; nothing from the spec's 'When no seed works' list is done.
decisions.why: The spec's Edge Cases and Assumptions name re-seeding as THE path when a map has no northwest-backed margin at its current seed ('its seed is a roll, not a fact about the place; its declared fall, water and other declared knobs are kept (Kashikawa's brook_side confluence included)'). Kashikawa is a pool map at the same footing as the other two: R4 records that at seed 3, on the fixed divided test and feature 230's order, no clean wind-facing margin was open and the belt came out with no trees - the very defect the GM asked about. Checked in the diff: kashikawa.gen.py changes seed=3 to seed=8 and adds the docstring; households=20, down_deg=315, water_sink='offmap', brook_side=-1 stand; R4 records the drain still ends by the brook (54-94 px against 83), so the confluence the spec names is kept. Choosing 8 over 14 among the five clean seeds is a choice among spec-permitted rolls, and it serves the request: a belt wrapped 333 degrees round the cluster is not 'to the north and west', and FR-010 names 'embracing the cluster' as a rule that must still hold. The 200-degree arc assertion in test_pool_wind.py is a test that fails only when the requested thing (the belt on the north and west) is absent - enforcement, not scope. Re-checked this round by re-running measure.py on the shipped manifests (after D8's re-roll): Kashikawa 20/20, seat_offwind false, seat_divided false, 281 belt clumps at 353 degrees, arc 169; all five maps match R5's table row for row. D4's own 264-at-288 / 134-degree figures are the seed-search observation (R4), not the shipped map. Inashiro keeps seed 4 (not a re-seed). One stale literal outside the plan: the test's comment says the pool's belts measured 87-171 degrees where R5 says 87-168. This round: the Summary now says three maps re-seeded on R1 and R4's measurements, matching D4 (R1: Sawada, Mizuguchi; R4: Kashikawa).

decisions.summary: seat_cluster's divided test took each brook-near band point's LATERAL half of the band, so a brook running behind the band parallel to the margin read as dividing it; brook_banks(), lifted to module level and unit-tested, takes the side of the nearest brook segment for each band point.
decisions.why: A defect found in this work and fixed in it (constitution XIV). It narrows nothing the request or spec asked for: it makes feature 230's strike-out - a rule FR-010 requires to still hold - test what that rule is for (houses on one bank), where it had been striking margins with every house on one bank (R4: Kashikawa 20 | 0, Inashiro 15 | 0). The rule's purpose is measured as kept under the fixed test: R4's cohort table records 0 houses on both banks and 0 structures across the brook under feature 230's order. Its effect on the request is in the request's favor: Inashiro seats wind-facing at its reference seed without a re-seed. brook_banks is present in cluster.py with tests in test_cluster.py and test_surface.py.

decisions.summary: Re-seeding lost the pool's only exhibit of four knob values (bamboo both, byre_form courtyard, copse_siting against_the_belt, lane_web alleys; R6), which the gate's coverage floor caught; each is declared on the map that showed it on main (Kashikawa bamboo=both, Mizuguchi byre_form=courtyard and copse_siting=against_the_belt, Sawada lane_web=alleys), by the mechanism Sawada's intake='open' already uses; HamletSpec gains byre_form, validated against and pinned onto the settlement engine's existing knob.
decisions.why: It narrows nothing the GM asked for. The request's only 'declared' constraint is the WIND ('none of our maps should have this declared'); no wind is declared, and the shipped manifests (re-read this round) record windward NW, wind_source regional, seat_offwind false and seat_divided false on all five, with measure.py reproducing R5 exactly. Against the spec: the Edge Case requires a re-seeded map's 'declared fall, water and other declared knobs' be kept - they are (seeds 8/27/24, falls, sinks, brook_side, intake unchanged in the diff). 'A declared knob changed' is in the 'When no seed works' list, which forbids departing from a map's declarations to RESCUE a northwest seat; D8 is neither in that case (every map found a clean wind-facing seed first) nor a departure from any existing declaration - it adds declarations whose values were not chosen for the wind but fixed by what each map showed on main (checked against origin/main's manifests: Kashikawa bamboo both; Mizuguchi courtyard, against_the_belt; Sawada alleys and courtyard). Its effect is to make each map differ from its pre-feature self in the wind and seat, which the GM asked to change, rather than in four unrelated knobs the re-roll happened to flip. It serves FR-006 ('each MUST pass the full gate' - the coverage floor failed without it) and the standing one-map-per-value knob rule the pool already enforces. HamletSpec.byre_form is the minimal mechanism for that: a validated field onto an existing settlement knob, one unit test, no new behavior. No wind rule moved (R5 re-measured).
